nodes.summary: For an instance $(n, E, K)$ of MINIMUM FILL-IN and a list $A$ of pairs of natural numbers, the augmented graph is the graph of the edge list $E$ followed by $A$ on $n$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$ or to $A$.
nodes.title: Graph augmented by added edges

nodes.summary: The decision problem MINIMUM FILL-IN accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an instance $(n, E, K)$ of MINIMUM FILL-IN that is well formed and feasible.
nodes.title: The MINIMUM FILL-IN (CHORDAL COMPLETION) problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of MINIMUM FILL-IN is feasible when there are an ordering $\sigma$ of the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ (a list that contains each of them exactly once) and a list $A$ of pairs of natural numbers, with no repeated entries and at most $K$ entries, such that every pair $(u, v)$ in $A$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, neither $(u, v)$ nor $(v, u)$ belongs to $E$, and $(v, u)$ does not…
nodes.title: Feasible MINIMUM FILL-IN instances

nodes.summary: An instance of MINIMUM FILL-IN is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edge list) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).
nodes.title: Instances of MINIMUM FILL-IN

nodes.summary: The decision problem MINIMUM FILL-IN lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to MINIMUM FILL-IN.
nodes.title: MINIMUM FILL-IN (CHORDAL COMPLETION) is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of MINIMUM FILL-IN is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reverse $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed MINIMUM FILL-IN instances

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
